narrative_purpose: Shows the coral holobiont: the reef-builder is an animal hosting photosynthetic algae inside its cells, and that partnership is the energy source for the skeleton.
subject: A magnified cutaway of a single coral polyp. The translucent tube-shaped animal body has a ring of fine tentacles at the top and sits on a pale aragonite skeleton cup below it. The tissue is densely packed with round golden-brown algal cells glowing softly. A gentle flow of small warm-gold particles drifts inward from the algae into the animal tissue (sugar); a fainter stream of pale bubbles drifts outward from the animal (waste gas). Below the polyp, fresh pale skeleton is visibly forming as a layered rim.
scene: Inside and just around one coral polyp, cool clear sunlit water above, dark skeleton cavity below.
camera: Tight macro cross-section, the single polyp filling most of the frame.
light: Sunlit teal from above, warm amber glow from the golden algae inside the tissue, cyan rim on the fresh skeleton.
palette: Ocean teal water, warm amber-gold algae, pale mineral skeleton, void indigo cavity.
style: Painterly microscopic naturalist plate, organic and glowing, not a vector infographic.
detail_level: Crisp on the polyp tissue, algal cells and skeleton rim; soft open water around it for labels.
composition: Central polyp with clear open regions upper-left and right for callouts marking algae, sugar flow, and forming skeleton.
consistency_notes: The golden cells are INSIDE the animal's tissue, not outside. Keep the amber-in-teal palette consistent with the zooxanthellae glossary look.
negative_prompt: no text, no labels, no arrows, no chemical formulas, no molecular diagrams, no photographic or 3D-render look, no cartoon style
